A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STAR-DSS research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original finetuning experiments, safety and capability evaluations, attack tests, ablations and preprocessing-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports revised preprocessing times with uncertainty values.

M1.justification: The guardrail-derived STAR scores, chunkwise weighting, cross-entropy/KL objective and reference-model regularization remain unchanged. The revised theoretical threshold discussion does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The training datasets, safety and capability benchmarks, and harmful-finetuning, response-adaptation, prompt-poisoning and prefilling scenarios are retained. Newly cited datasets and attacks do not introduce additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator memberships remain unchanged across corresponding main-text and appendix experiments. Panacea and Booster are added as related-work citations, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported data mixtures, metrics, model configurations and training hyperparameters remain unchanged, including v1 Table 8 versus v2 Table 6. The new judge template discloses evaluation details without documenting a changed procedure.

E4.justification: The existing analysis of preprocessing cost across chunk sizes and guardrails receives revised timing evidence in Table 3. Safety ablations, robustness tests and qualitative attack examples otherwise remain unchanged after matching their relocated appendices.

E5.justification: v2 adds plus/minus uncertainty values to all timing entries in Table 3, where v1 reports point estimates. Run counts and the meaning of these uncertainty values are unspecified; safety and capability tables retain point estimates.

E6.justification: All 16 preprocessing-time entries in Table 3 change. For example, Granite Guardian-3.1-2B on 100 PureBad samples at M=1 changes from 1.92 to 1.15 ± 0.01 minutes under the same stated hardware setup. Safety and capability scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly indexes the guardrail error by τ, states threshold independence and changes the FN supremum. Appendix A also changes the pointwise Pinsker statement to a supremum over prompts while leaving its right-hand side prompt-dependent. Its added STAR≥τ restriction conflicts with the lemma's application in A.3; the overall bound remains structurally unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain dynamic safety shaping, partial-response STAR assessment and STAR-DSS safety preservation without sacrificing capability. The introduction retains the same 20.41% improvement claim and theoretical-guarantee framing.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds guidance on compact guardrails and policy-dependent selection, while largely consolidating existing cost and robustness discussion. Section 6.3 adds a benchmark-policy explanation for the ranking depicted in Figure 4, although that ranking conflicts with unchanged Table 11.

D1.justification: v2 announces public code access and adds the full GPT-as-a-judge evaluation template in Appendix L. v1 identifies GPT-4o as the judge without supplying this template. Existing implementation and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds eight cited works, including GuardSet-X, adaptive and prefilling jailbreak research, Panacea and Booster. The principal static-versus-dynamic positioning and relationship to Deep Token remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The appendices are extensively reorganized: former A–C become subsections of A, the worked prompt moves from J to B, and ablations move from D to K. A discussion and limitations section and a NeurIPS checklist are added, although most existing main-text prose is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves earlier and gains a fuller caption explaining colors and markers. Table 2 changes to a text-wrapped layout, timing Table 3 moves into the main text, and a judge-template box is added. Existing plots and benchmark-table designs are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility documentation through code-access information and the complete judge template, and adds timing uncertainty reporting. However, its proof edits introduce an unsupported supremum and inconsistent STAR-threshold conditions in Appendix A. The added guardrail interpretation also leaves the existing Figure 4/Table 11 discrepancy unresolved. These documentation gains coexist with reduced theoretical reliability, preventing a clear net quality judgment.
